question: How many UNESCO Natural World Heritage sites are there in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **seven UNESCO Natural World Heritage sites** in India.
 
• These sites are considered to be of **outstanding universal value** and are protected by** international treaties. **
 
• The seven sites are: **Kaziranga National Park, Manas Wildlife Sanctuary, Keoladeo National Park, Sundarbans National Park, Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks, Western Ghats, and Great Himalayan National Park.**
 
• These sites are chosen based on their **natural beauty, exceptional biodiversity, geological significance**, and **cultural importance.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Through international collaboration in** education, the arts, sciences, and culture, **the** United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) **works to advance **world peace and security.**
 
• It has partners in the non-governmental, intergovernmental, and private sectors in addition to its **194 member **states and **12 associate members. **
 
• **53 regional field offices **and** 199 national commissions **help UNESCO, which has its main office in **Paris, France**, carry out its global mandate.
 
• In** 1945, UNESCO **was established.
